Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The umpires and players are all out in the middle and the new opening pair of Jake Fraser-McGurk and Matthew Short are set to start for Australia! Shaheen Afridi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go! It will be Afridi to Short first up! Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ....

Australia rotated through eight bowlers, with Mitchell Starc leading the charge, claiming three crucial wickets that set the tone for their dominant performance. The rest of the attack chipped in effectively, but the last 20-30 minutes allowed Pakistan some breathing room, which may sting a bit. With a target of 204 runs, Australia will back themselves to get the job done, yet Pakistan’s fierce bowling attack has the potential to make this chase challenging. Early breakthroughs will be essential for Pakistan to stay in the hunt, while Australia’s new opening pair will look to lay a solid foundation. We’re in for an exciting chase!

Shaheen Afridi chipped in with an entertaining cameo, but his stay was short-lived, ending with a clean strike from Starc. The tail, however, showed resilience, Naseem Shah and Irfan Khan forged a 27-run stand, and Naseem's spirited counterattack against spin kept the scoreboard ticking despite wickets falling around him. His late heroics lifted Pakistan to a total of 203, a score that had seemed far out of reach for much of the innings.

Babar Azam entered with confidence, showcasing his class with a few elegant strokes to settle Pakistan's nerves. While Mohammad Rizwan initially struggled to find his rhythm, the pair weathered the early onslaught and began building a promising partnership. However, the introduction of Adam Zampa disrupted Pakistan’s momentum, as he claimed the crucial wicket of Babar, further tightening Australia’s grip on the innings.

Australia put on a fantastic display with the ball, bowling the visitors out for a modest 203 runs. Although they might have aimed to keep Pakistan to an even lower total, this target is one Australia will feel confident chasing. They fully capitalized on winning the toss and opting to bowl, with Mitchell Starc setting the tone brilliantly from the outset, supported seamlessly by skipper Pat Cummins. Starc struck early, dismissing debutant Saim Ayub in his second over and following it up with the wicket of the other opener Abdullah Shafique just a few overs later.

Naseem Shah’s late heroics have transformed Pakistan’s innings, pushing their total past 200 and giving them something to compete with the ball. This knock will certainly inject some momentum into Pakistan's camp and they will hope to carry it on with the ball in hand.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks has been called for! Australia have tightened the screws expertly, dismantling Pakistan’s middle order to seize firm control of the game. The crucial wicket of Mohammad Rizwan has swung the momentum even further in their favour, and they’ll now be eager to mop up the tail quickly. For Pakistan, it's been a challenging innings, with wickets falling just as they seemed to be finding stability. All hopes now rest on Irfan Khan to push the total forward and give the bowlers something to defend. With that Shaheen Afridi walks out to bat next.

Pakistan enter this series with a fresh sense of purpose and change. With Mohammad Rizwan stepping up as captain, the team is hopeful for the beginning of a new era, one that revives the fierce dominance Pakistan once commanded on the world stage. They’re strengthened by the return of superstar Babar Azam and pace sensation Shaheen Afridi, both eager to make a significant impact and live up to the high expectations of fans worldwide. Saim Ayub and Irfan Khan are set to debut in ODIs for the side. Pakistan's bowling attack, long a defining strength, is primed to unleash its full potential on these Australian pitches, where pace and skill are bound to shine. The stage couldn’t be more perfectly set for this clash, and we’re just moments away from the toss. Sit back and brace up for an electrifying contest!

Australia, led by Pat Cummins, may be missing key figures like Mitchell Marsh and star opener Travis Head to paternity leave, but they’re fielding a lineup full of depth and young talent eager to make an impression. This ODI series is an ideal chance for Australia to resolve a few unanswered questions in their 50-over approach, making it vital for them to nail down their best combinations. Local heroes Jake Fraser-McGurk and Matthew Short form Australia’s sixth different ODI opening pair in as many games. Although the last 5 changes were a necessary adaptation after injuries and illnesses shuffled the squad during their recent series against England. Despite the hurdles, Australia boast a formidable squad on paper, blending experience with fresh energy, making them tough to beat. But they’re up against a spirited Pakistan team determined to turn each moment into a fierce contest.

The international cricketing calendar is stacked as we head into the final two months of 2024 and it is now time for the Australian summer to kick off! Australia now welcome Pakistan for a white-ball tour which will see 3 ODIs and 3 T20Is played before the crucial Border-Gavaskar Trophy starting in late November. The ODI series is up first and the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) will host the series opener and it could be an audition for individuals on both sides, especially Australia for the Champions Trophy early next year. Australia have had a month's break after their white-ball exploits in the UK and Pakistan last played a white-ball match way back in the infamous 2024 T20 World Cup campaign which means both sides will be a bit undercooked in the ODI format to begin with. Starting with team news, regular skipper Mitchell Marsh and marquee opener Travis Head are both absent due to paternity leave and Cameron Green, who was having a fantastic 2024, is recovering from an injury which opens the doors for a few fringe players. Pat Cummins will lead the side that does still feature a stacked lineup which includes the likes of Steven Smith, Mitchell Starc, and Marcus Stoinis just to name a few. The big question is who gets an opportunity at the top and this series could well decide Head's opener partner for next year's Champions Trophy. The likes of Jake Fraser-McGurk, Matthew Short and Cooper Connolly will all be itching to make a name for themselves. The pace attack seems well-rounded and there are a lot of options in the all-rounders' department as well with Aaron Hardie making a real name for himself and Glenn Maxwell will be looking to get back to his best as he has seen a real dip in form after that resounding ODI World Cup win in 2023. Moving on to Pakistan, they will be led by Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam who was axed for the last two Tests against England is back in the side. Just like the Aussies, Pakistan too have a stacked pace attack and they will be happy to move on from the flat pitches of Pakistan to the pace and bounce of Australia as Shaheen Afridi and co look to make their mark. Aamer Jamal had a memorable time when Pakistan last came to Australia for the Test matches about a year ago but it will be a series of finding some lost form for the likes of Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf. The batting lineup will once again be tested with the likes of Saim Ayub, Kamran Ghulam and others still finding their feet in international cricket. Young Arafat Minhas who played for Pakistan in the last Under-19 World Cup also gets a spot in the squad and it will be exciting to watch what the youngster can bring to the team. Also, both teams have announced their Playing XIs almost a day prior to the game and there are not many surprises from Australia with  Matthew Short and Jake Fraser-McGurk set to open the innings. As for Pakistan, Irfan Khan will make his debut in the middle order and they have gone for four frontline pacers in Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, Mohammad Hasnain and Haris Rauf. All in all, Australia might be missing a few key players but still have plenty of firepower, especially in home conditions to kick things off with a win. However, a few of the Pakistan players, mostly the batters are coming off that comeback Test series win against England which should bolster their confidence and the pacers will definitely present a stern challenge to the hosts as well. It should be a cracking curtain raiser at the M.C.G. Who are you backing for the win?
